content.text: The text is an anthology of literary excerpts, scholarly notes, poetry, and natural-history essays. It includes Ovidian footnotes, Dante’s descent through Hell, animal behavior, birds, insects, fossils, water, eyesight, and wildlife conservation. A major narrative follows abducted women who secure release through Elaine Cavendish’s $200,000 check, while Croyden and Macloud later find Parmenter’s jewels in a Hampton cellar. Another story follows priest Jose in Simiti, Colombia: he confronts plague panic, protects Carmen, discovers gold hidden behind an altar in an abandoned hilltop church, and plans escape to America. Carmen is abducted to Banco, where Ana protects her from Diego; they flee aboard a steamboat and return by canoe toward Simiti. The text closes with discussions of faith, fear, spiritual healing, and Carmen’s influence on Jose.
